To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we develop surrogate scoring rules (SSR) to extend strictly proper scoring rules (2) we use SSR to develop the uniform dominant truth serum (DTS) for multi-task peer prediction, (3) DTS achieves truthfulness in dominant strategies, and (4) our results are verified both theoretically and experimentally.

(1) we introduce the concept of surrogate scoring rule (SSR) that extends strictly proper scoring rules (2) we show that a uniform dominant truth serum (DTS) is strictly proper and truthful in uniform dominant strategy when the number of tasks and agents is large

(i) we introduce surrogate scoring rules (SSR) that can quantify the value of information when the ground truth is not available, (ii) we show that SSR preserves strict properness of strictly proper scoring rules, and (iii) we introduce uniform dominant truth serum (DTS) that is a strict proper mechanism that is truthful in uniform dominant strategy in a multi task peer prediction setting when agents adopt same strategy across all tasks they are assigned
In summary, our research is concerned with
designing scoring rules that are strictly proper in settings where ground truth is not available.
the design of mechanisms to elicit information from strategic agents in a variety of settings.
designing scoring rules for settings with no ground truth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper proposes and studies surrogate scoring rules, and uniform dominant truth serum, which are two new tools for eliciting private information from strategic individuals in the absence of access to ground truth signals, with the goal of achieving strict properness.
we propose a new scoring rule for multi-task peer prediction, that can be shown to be strictly proper, and that is also empirically effective.

we propose a novel mechanism design framework to elicit information from strategic agents, and develop a multi task mechanism called DTS that can achieve strict properness even when the mechanism designer does not know the ground truth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we introduce a new scoring rule that preserves the desirable properties of proper scoring rules in a setting without ground truth, and use the new scoring rule to design a new multi task peer prediction mechanism with strong incentive guarantees.

we develop a novel mechanism to achieve truthfulness in dominant strategy in a multi task peer prediction setting, and we also introduce a novel scoring rule that can be used in a variety of settings to quantify the value of information without access to ground truth.
we introduce surrogate scoring rules to quantify quality of elicited private information when the mechanism designer does not know the ground truth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of information elicited from agents can be quantified even when there is no ground truth.
when the mechanism designer does not know the ground truth, it is still possible to design incentive mechanisms that elicit high quality information.
, even when the ground truth is not available, the quality of information elicited by a mechanism can still be evaluated and improved.
